From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook. I have read the Seller's documents as the other side's position, not as instructions.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The Seller's preamble says its positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "marked FINAL" and are "not intended to be re-opened." It also says 10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "standard market."

**We should reject this framing outright.**
- Under our playbook, the 20% cap and 18-month period are fallbacks. Each needs **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft**. No such authority has been given. A counterparty saying something was agreed at principal level is not that authority.
- If anyone on our side believes Amelia did agree something, confirm it directly with her in writing before relying on it. Until then, every point below is open.
- The "market" claims are the Seller's advocacy. They are unsupported and do not override our mandate.

**Recommended response:** "We do not agree that any position is settled or final. Our mark-up follows."

---

## 1. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Gap and pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only with written Amelia Frost authority (none given) | **Reject.** Re-state 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not offer the fallback. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. Reject. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only ("deductible") | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** once exceeded ("tipping") | Two departures: 5x the amount, and a deductible instead of a tipping basket. A deductible permanently removes AUD 250k of recovery. Reject both. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs written Amelia Frost approval (none) | Reject. Re-state 24 months. |

### Hidden general-regime override (cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5)
This is the most dangerous drafting in the package. Two provisions combine:
- "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise**"; and
- limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to **all Claims of any nature**."

Read together, these would push **title, capacity, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment/price obligations, covenants and fraud** into the general cap, thresholds and time limits by default. That breaches two playbook rules:
1. **Categories must stay separate, with no hidden general-regime override.** The default should be the reverse: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, unless expressly stated.
2. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out** of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. The Seller's draft does not carve fraud out at all. "All Claims of any nature" on its face captures it. This is non-negotiable. Under the playbook, no one can waive it.

**Pushback:**
- Delete "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- Limit cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 to general Warranty Claims.
- Insert an overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that expressly prevails over cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5.

### Fundamental / Title warranties
The Seller wants capacity and title on the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." **Reject.** The playbook requires:
- a separate regime with a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
- a claims period of at least six years; and
- exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

Title is the core of what we are buying. If title fails, a 20% cap means we pay AUD 24m and can recover at most AUD 4.8m.

### Tax / IP
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime above." **Not accepted.** Under our playbook, Tax and IP terms remain **open**. Neither side has agreed to unlimited liability, and nothing has been resolved. The Seller's statement would quietly put tax and IP inside the 20%/18-month regime. Respond that these are open, will be dealt with separately, and are not covered by cl 12.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### General disclosure (Schedule 7, DL 1.1–1.2)
The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." This is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure that the playbook rejects.

**Pushback:**
- Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2.
- Disclosure should qualify warranties only where a matter is **specifically and fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify its nature and scope, against the specific warranty.

Note also that DL 1.4 says nothing admits breach, liability or that any consent is required. That is acceptable as a non-admission clause. It must not, however, be read to dilute the specific disclosures. Those disclosures are helpful to us: they expressly confirm the open Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and bonus issues.

### Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, **including any matter discoverable** from the data room or public records." This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion with constructive knowledge on top. It is worse than a standard anti-sandbagging clause.

**Pushback:**
- Delete cl 8.3.
- If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a **seller-side** qualifier limited to **named seller knowledge persons**, after **reasonable enquiry**.
- It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
This is a material customer: about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue (DD-002). The Seller offers:
- **reasonable endeavours** only; and
- the condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."

DL 2 admits that no final consent has been provided and there is no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. This fails the playbook on both counts. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent, and consent-on-delivery is expressly rejected.

**Pushback:**
- Make it a **condition precedent** to Completion: an **effective** written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, **plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.
- Delivery to the Buyer must occur before Completion.
- Add a Buyer-only waiver right and a corresponding Seller obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours.

### Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
About AUD 3.2m is outstanding (DD-003). It has change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Seller offers a release "following Completion." DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.

**Pushback:** Require all of the following:
- a **current payout letter**;
- **direct repayment from Completion funds**, as a funds-flow line item, with the amount deducted as Debt on a debt-free basis; and
- **effective security releases** delivered at Completion. This includes any PPSR discharges and deeds of release.

A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from the lender **and** Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither exists, so do not concede it.

### Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses
The Seller states the AUD 420,000 bonuses "are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised." DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow, and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. This is the "silent exclusion" the playbook warns against. These bonuses are triggered by Completion and are company obligations. If they are not dealt with, the Company (and so the Buyer) bears them after Completion.

**Pushback:** Either:
- add a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs** (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation where applicable), treated as Debt or a transaction expense deducted from price; or
- make the bonuses expressly Seller-funded, with an indemnity.

Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost figure. Do not assume one.

---

## 4. Specific matters

### Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
The Seller wants the indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment." DL 4 confirms the following:
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Pushback:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own, or validly hold rights in, the Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party claims, replacement and re-development costs, and the consequences of non-transfer.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

**Caveat:** The AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified either way**. DD-010 is an internal record. Do not assert in correspondence that AUD 180k is owed, or that it is the full exposure. Ask the Seller for bank evidence and Ironquay's confirmation of the balance.

### DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." DL 6 records the following:
- a download link was sent to an unintended external address;
- the file may contain about 1,240 records;
- it is not established whether the file was accessed or what its scope was; and
- it is not established whether notification is required.

**Our position:** Assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum. Equally, do not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation.

**Pushback:**
- Add covenants to **preserve logs** and evidence.
- Require the Seller to complete a proper investigation and give **regular written updates** before Completion, including access logs, link-expiry status and any recipient confirmation of deletion.
- Require the Seller to assess its notification obligations under the Privacy Act, consult the Buyer, and obtain Buyer approval of any notification or communication.
- Add a specific warranty or indemnity for losses arising from the incident.
- Delete the "not material" language.

Do not put a number on this in either direction.

### Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 is silent on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and says DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.

**Our position:** Assess. Request the contracts, renewal and termination terms, accrual treatment, and how the renewals relate to each other. Classify them once the facts are known. **Do not** automatically treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Equally, **do not** accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label without evidence.

### Title (DD-012)
The Seller says title "is evidenced by the share register at DD-012." DL 10 itself concedes this is only "the source relied on" and not Buyer verification. The register is an internal document supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof.

**Require independent evidence:**
- ASIC current and historical extracts;
- the constitution and all share issue and transfer records;
- original share certificates;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and Company;
- confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or other rights to shares;
- releases of any encumbrances; and
- Seller board approval and authority.

All of this should be backed by fundamental warranties under the separate regime described in section 1.

---

## 5. Additional points (not in the playbook; recommended diligence)

- **Stale disclosure date.** The Disclosure Letter is as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. We need a brought-down or updated Disclosure Letter and confirmation that no new matters have arisen. This matters particularly for Bluefen, Riverlark and DD-006. Any supplementary disclosure before Completion must not cure warranty breaches without our consent.
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller says the lease needs notification only and Mossvale has an assignment restriction but no change-of-control consent. Our counsel should **verify these readings against the source documents** rather than rely on the Seller's characterisation. Add the lease notification as a Completion deliverable or covenant.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing.** No Amelia Frost written authority exists for any fallback. Verify with her directly if anyone suggests otherwise.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m (not 20%).
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5k, basket AUD 50k, **tipping** from the first dollar (not AUD 25k/250k deductible).
4. **General claims period:** 24 months (not 18).
5. **Remove the hidden general-regime override.** General limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate.
6. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
7. **Fundamental / Title:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
8. **Disclosure:** delete general data-room and public-register disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only.
9. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Use only named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
10. **Bluefen:** condition precedent requiring an effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 is satisfied, before Completion. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
11. **Riverlark:** current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and security releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and do not treat AUD 180k as verified.
14. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants plus a specific protection. No assumed breach or quantum, and delete "not material."
15. **Sandbar:** diligence first. No automatic Debt treatment or deduction, and no acceptance of the "ordinary course" label.
16. **Tax / IP:** remain open and are not settled under the general regime.
17. **Title:** independent evidence required. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
18. **Bring-down:** require an updated Disclosure Letter, and verify the lease and Mossvale readings.

**Overall:** The Seller's draft departs from our playbook on essentially every liability point. It also contains two structural traps: the "all Claims" override, which captures fraud and title, and blanket deemed disclosure combined with constructive buyer knowledge. Together these could largely remove our recourse. Those structural points should lead our mark-up, ahead of the headline numbers.

- **direct repayment from Completion funds**, as a funds-flow line item, with the amount deducted as Debt on a debt-free basis; and
- **effective security releases** delivered at Completion. This includes any PPSR discharges and deeds of release.

A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from the lender **and** Amelia Frost's written approval. Neither exists, so do not concede it.

### Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses
The Seller states the AUD 420,000 bonuses "are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised." DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow, and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. This is the "silent exclusion" the playbook warns against. These bonuses are triggered by Completion and are company obligations. If they are not dealt with, the Company (and so the Buyer) bears them after Completion.

**Pushback:** Either:
- add a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs** (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation where applicable), treated as Debt or a transaction expense deducted from price; or
- make the bonuses expressly Seller-funded, with an indemnity.

Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost figure. Do not assume one.

## 4. Specific matters

### Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
The Seller wants the indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment." DL 4 confirms the following:
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Pushback:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own, or validly hold rights in, the Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party claims, replacement and re-development costs, and the consequences of non-transfer.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

**Caveat:** The AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified either way**. DD-010 is an internal record. Do not assert in correspondence that AUD 180k is owed, or that it is the full exposure. Ask the Seller for bank evidence and Ironquay's confirmation of the balance.

### DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." DL 6 records the following:
- a download link was sent to an unintended external address;
- the file may contain about 1,240 records;
- it is not established whether the file was accessed or what its scope was; and
- it is not established whether notification is required.

**Our position:** Assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum. Equally, do not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation.

**Pushback:**
- Add covenants to **preserve logs** and evidence.
- Require the Seller to complete a proper investigation and give **regular written updates** before Completion, including access logs, link-expiry status and any recipient confirmation of deletion.
- Require the Seller to assess its notification obligations under the Privacy Act, consult the Buyer, and obtain Buyer approval of any notification or communication.
- Add a specific warranty or indemnity for losses arising from the incident.
- Delete the "not material" language.

Do not put a number on this in either direction.

### Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 is silent on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and says DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.

**Our position:** Assess. Request the contracts, renewal and termination terms, accrual treatment, and how the renewals relate to each other. Classify them once the facts are known. **Do not** automatically treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Equally, **do not** accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label without evidence.

### Title (DD-012)
The Seller says title "is evidenced by the share register at DD-012." DL 10 itself concedes this is only "the source relied on" and not Buyer verification. The register is an internal document supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof.

**Require independent evidence:**
- ASIC current and historical extracts;
- the constitution and all share issue and transfer records;
- original share certificates;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and Company;
- confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or other rights to shares;
- releases of any encumbrances; and
- Seller board approval and authority.

All of this should be backed by fundamental warranties under the separate regime described in section 1.

## 6. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing.** No Amelia Frost written authority exists for any fallback. Verify with her directly if anyone suggests otherwise.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m (not 20%).
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5k, basket AUD 50k, **tipping** from the first dollar (not AUD 25k/250k deductible).
4. **General claims period:** 24 months (not 18).
5. **Remove the hidden general-regime override.** General limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate.
6. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
7. **Fundamental / Title:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
8. **Disclosure:** delete general data-room and public-register disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only.
9. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Use only named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
10. **Bluefen:** condition precedent requiring an effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 is satisfied, before Completion. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
11. **Riverlark:** current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and security releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and do not treat AUD 180k as verified.
14. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants plus a specific protection. No assumed breach or quantum, and delete "not material."
15. **Sandbar:** diligence first. No automatic Debt treatment or deduction, and no acceptance of the "ordinary course" label.
16. **Tax / IP:** remain open and are not settled under the general regime.
17. **Title:** independent evidence required. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
18. **Bring-down:** require an updated Disclosure Letter, and verify the lease and Mossvale readings.

**Overall:** The Seller's draft departs from our playbook on essentially every liability point. It also contains two structural traps: the "all Claims" override, which captures fraud and title, and blanket deemed disclosure combined with constructive buyer knowledge. Together these could largely remove our recourse. Those structural points should lead our mark-up, ahead of the headline numbers.
